title: Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems
read_depth: Read the relevant statements and surrounding derivations in sections 2.2, 2.4 and 2.6; not a full-book reading.
source_locations: Section 2.2, Theorem 2.2, printed page 38 (PDF page index 48): local existence and uniqueness
Section 2.4, Theorem 2.10, printed page 46 (PDF page index 56): smooth dependence and variational equations
Section 2.4, Theorem 2.11, printed page 47 (PDF page index 57): parameter dependence
Section 2.6, Theorem 2.13, printed page 51 (PDF page index 61): maximal solution
Section 2.6, Lemma 2.14 and Corollary 2.15, printed page 52 (PDF page index 62): continuation from compact sets
use: Standard ODE existence, continuation and parameter-dependence inputs; the project's energy and denominator estimates are derived independently in theorem_advisor.md.
limitation: A finite-dimensional ODE theorem does not establish a continuum field-theory limit, physically correct renormalization, quantum fluctuation validity or all-time response stability.

title: DLMF 5.9.15: Binet integral for the digamma function
authors: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
read_depth: Read equation 5.9.15, its domain Re(z)>0, and the note identifying it as the differentiated form of Binet's formula.
use: Positive integral representation of log(z)-1/(2z)-psi(z), proving matched chi_b>0 after the recurrence substitution.
limitation: Proves a special-function sign under positive real z; it is not an independent derivation of the physical matching prescription.

title: DLMF 5.5.2: Digamma recurrence
authors: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
read_depth: Read equation 5.5.2 and its recurrence-section context.
use: Transforms psi(1+z) to psi(z)+1/z in the susceptibility positivity proof.
limitation: The application here is restricted to positive real z and does not use analytic continuation near digamma poles.

title: DLMF 3.5(v): Gauss quadrature
authors: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
read_depth: Read positivity of the Christoffel weights after equation 3.5.18, polynomial exactness at equation 3.5.20_1, and the Gauss-Legendre specialization 3.5.21.
use: Exact positive longitudinal quadrature weights sum to the interval length, supplying the analytic global Z bound at fixed K=20 and n=0 through4.
limitation: Exact polynomial quadrature identities do not hold literally for rounded weights; a separate exact rational certificate was checked for the generated coefficient list.

title: 2022 CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants
read_depth: Read the alpha and inverse-alpha entries in the two-page table; did not audit the underlying measurement adjustment.
source_locations: Fine-structure constant and inverse fine-structure constant rows
use: Context check: the recommended alpha central value 7.2973525643e-3 also obeys the broad alpha<1/137 inequality.
limitation: The theorem uses a declared parameter inequality, not a mathematical proof of a measured physical constant. The frozen production source retains alpha=1/137.035999084 and was not modified.

title: Frozen round-4 P3 contract, implementation and acceptance
read_depth: Read the complete response contract and acceptance JSON; inspected the grid, susceptibility and current definitions in response.py and the inherited constants. Executed only the coefficient construction and exact-rational inequality checks; did not rerun the trajectory.
use: Freezes the physical and computational model to which the conditional theorem is applied.
limitation: Recorded response errors are sampled numerical comparisons. The conditional theorem does not turn those comparisons into interval enclosures.

exact_rounded_coefficient_certificate.meaning: Exact rational certificate for the real ODE whose constants equal the generated IEEE coefficient values; not an interval time-step certificate.
